items.after:
Replace it with a recursive-backtracker maze over a node lattice, giving 1-wide corridors between 1-wide walls:

- Nodes sit at odd row / odd col; all nodes are path. A randomized DFS carves a spanning tree of corridors (at odd/even or even/odd cells) between nodes.
- (even, even) cells are never carved, so no 2×2 block is all-path — hence no plaza, and nothing approaching the 3×2 limit. Dead-ends (degree-1), T-intersections (degree-3) and occasional crossings occur naturally; ~88% of path cells are degree-2 corridors.
- The Exit is placed on the border directly in front of a node (top/bottom at odd col, left/right at odd row), so it connects straight into the maze.
- `GRID_COLS` changes 20 → 21 so both dimensions are odd and the border forms a clean wall ring; the canvas auto-resizes to 672×480 via `main.js`.

Done when: reloading shows winding corridors instead of a blob. Verified by a script that generates many maps and checks connectivity, border-exit placement, and that no 2×2 all-path block exists.
items.before: `generateMap` grows a blob: starting from a border Exit, it repeatedly carves a random obstacle adjacent to any existing path cell until 65% of cells are path. Most path cells end up surrounded by 3–4 other path cells, so the map reads as one large field, not paths.
